itemTryRelease with force one rejects ownership states 4 and 5; valid states 0 through 3 proceed. Player ownership (1) clears gPlayerHeldItemHandle at 0x800EF724. Actor ownership (2 or 3) resolves the owner handle and clears the live owner ActorScriptState.heldItemHandle at offset 0x190, including when the owner is the caller. A missing owner does not prevent release. Every live owner has a valid, stable actor-layout held-item field. Owner lookup does not establish runtime kind, so that layout is an explicit prerequisite.

Use the original 166-entry ItemKind.release column at offset 0x48. Only kind 49 selects lightBulbResetReleasedGlow at 0x80123140, and kind 80 selects baseballCapResetReleasedScale at 0x80123060; all other release hooks are null. Arbitrary callback substitution is excluded. These hooks inspect ownership before release resets it: only Pikachu ownership (2) triggers the bulb material-animation reset to 0xF3 or the cap scale reset to one. Hold, launch, collision and update hooks are not invoked by this native.

The cap callback calls itemSetScale, which restores the root radius from state.baseRadius, sets uniform scale to area.objectScale multiplied by the catalog scale, then recursively scales and halves root and child bounds. Area and catalog scales and bounds must be initialized and finite, and the hierarchy must be acyclic. This describes the helper’s writes; it does not promise that every child bound returns to its original value. The bulb callback initializes the material track from borrowed animation program 0xF3 and sets its active halfword to one. That program must be valid, its jumps must terminate, interpolation must be representable, and interpolation duration must be nonzero. Evaluation with step zero is deterministic and performs no RNG update, allocation or callback.

A release callback receives the item and former holder address by value. Both retail hooks ignore the holder argument and retain no C-stack pointer. After the hook, release writes world ownership (0), owner zero, modeTime zero and ground-and-air mode (0), then clears the transfer-permission bit. Mode zero recursively clears hierarchy flags 0x700 only when the root has at least one of those bits; otherwise child-only bits remain unchanged. Release performs no collision registration, unregister operation, search-tree mutation, item-count change or resource free.

No item allocation, deletion, physical attachment-matrix update, hold callback, game-mode change, message, audio operation, OS queue operation or DMA occurs synchronously. Items remain live borrowed objects whose ownership fields have changed; returning does not extend their lifetimes. Future held-item, update and rendering callbacks and their borrowed animation or model resources are outside this immediate footprint and require independent lifetime checks. Original SDK memory-primitive semantics and strict matching authentication remain required. No runtime claim is made.

A resolved candidate must be a genuine initialized runtime item with stable ItemStatePrefix and catalog kind zero through 165. The available resolver rejects zero, missing, destruction-marked and toolbox-owned items, but does not enforce item type. Arbitrary non-item objects are unsupported. The object pool is initialized with positive capacity and valid acyclic chains; lookup writes only local predecessor output.

Force one bypasses transfer-permission gating for eligible ownership states. Suspended ownership (5) still returns zero without releasing; toolbox ownership (4) is already excluded by the resolver. World ownership can return one and invoke its fixed retail release hook even if not currently held. The native reports itemTryRelease success directly rather than returning item kind, and does not perform pickup or replacement.

callbacks.result_semantics: Consume item handle, count, lifetime, radial scale and particle scale. For an available item, start its visual direction motion and allocate/register the requested particle cluster; otherwise skip those effects. Append integer 0 in either case.
preconditions: The caller RuntimeObjectPrefix, ActorScriptState, captured VM, program and owned value buffer remain live and stable. Five operands lie above every protected local/frame record, bottom-to-top item handle, particle count, lifetime, radial scale and particle scale. Pop order is particle scale, radial scale, lifetime, count, handle. Integer conversion accepts integer/code-reference s32 or finite f32 with a representable truncated s32 result. Float conversion accepts f32 or signed integer/code-reference values. The post-pop depth has room for one integer result. All writable item, heap, pool, hierarchy, RNG and native-stack storage is disjoint from the protected VM/context/value/program regions. No concurrent mutation, destruction sweep, callback reentry or context replacement occurs.

Availability lookup uses the initialized positive-capacity object-handle pool with valid acyclic hash chains and live records. It reads without LRU, cursor, free-list or splay mutation. Zero, missing, destruction-marked and toolbox-owned runtime item handles are unavailable; the wrapper still consumes five operands and pushes 0 in those cases. Every nonnull result must be a live initialized runtime item kind 0x86 with complete 0xF0 ItemState storage, not just ItemStatePrefix. The wrapper does not validate arbitrary other runtime kinds. Source position and handle remain readable throughout creation; storing the scalar target handle does not extend source lifetime.

For an available item, particle count is strictly positive. Count 0 or a negative count leaves the previous-element pointer null and is not safe. Let N = count + 2. The count loops, count * 3, count * 24 + 240, N * 128, all 64-byte matrix offsets, pointer additions and allocation rounding/header sizes fit their signed/unsigned target domains without overflow. N and object-handle increments fit s32; gActiveObjectHierarchyCount + 1 is representable. Enough native recursion stack exists for the created acyclic hierarchy. Finite lifetime, radial scale, particle scale and source coordinates are supplied; ordinary timed animation/effect expiry additionally expects a positive lifetime. This wrapper does not validate or clamp those scalar values.

itemStartDirectionMotion always stores idleMotionDelay = 5.5 at item state +0x68. If flags bit 0x8000 is set, direction storage is unchanged. Otherwise direction.poseIndex is initialized to 0 or 1. Only the three signed normal bytes at offsets 0x10 and 0x20 of the opposite 0x28-byte pose are overwritten from pitch -40 and yaw 0; other pose bytes and poseIndex remain unchanged. Direction mode becomes TIMED (1), duration and remaining receive lifetime, and two DirectionAngularMotion records receive angles evaluated from the current pose plus pitchRate 100 and yawRate 1000. The local rates array is consumed synchronously and no pointer to it is retained.

Direction math reads the current pose signed bytes as values scaled by 1/127, negates them, and evaluates opposite look angles. Those bounded vectors use original inline sqrt/abs instructions and readonly degree lookup tables, with explicit near-zero and vertical-vector branches. Original gMathAsinLookupTable entries 0..1024 and gMathQuarterSineLookupTable entries 0..512 are readable and unchanged. The fixed -40/0 and cosine +90 conversions fit s32; normal packing truncates finite bounded components into signed bytes. Only the two item motion records, next-pose normal bytes, mode/duration/remaining and native-stack output are written; no direction update callback or later per-frame animation runs here.

The original three complete 0x38-byte templates at 80078030, 80078068 and 800780A0 remain borrowed and unchanged. They have null child/sibling links and runtime kinds 169, 170 and 171. Their original six-word callback records at 80079118, 80079130 and 80079148 are retained. Immediate initialization is exactly effectEmitterInitialize at 8001968C for kind 169, null for kind 170, and particleClusterRendererInitialize at 80019834 for kind 171. No arbitrary initializer substitution is admitted. Deferred update/destruction/drawing pointers are borrowed lifetime obligations, not callbacks executed by this native.

Game heap storage is an initialized aligned circular block chain with truthful sizes, magic/tags and reciprocal links. Every selected block, split header, free-list and new allocation stays wholly within owned heap storage; all original rounding and metadata arithmetic is representable. Successful allocations are required for N objects of 0x68 bytes, one 0x18-byte root EffectEmitterState, one 0x0C-byte renderer ValueTrack, one count * 24 + 240 display list and one N * 128 matrix allocation: count + 6 successful allocation requests in total. Constructors do not safely handle allocation failure. All newly owned payload and allocator metadata are disjoint from live source/caller/VM/program/resources; existing allocator metadata may be updated as in the unchanged full heap closure.

The object-handle keyed pool has enough free entries for all N objects, consistent free/hash/ordered membership and stable initialized backing. Generated positive handles are unique and next-ID increment does not overflow. Existing ordered/hash links and pool metadata can change. The active-hierarchy NodePool has one free node with valid head/tail/free links. The object search tree is live, acyclic and correctly ordered with the original objectCompareSearchTreeOrder; insertion can splay and relink existing nodes. No handle/pool/heap allocation failure or concurrent registry traversal is admitted.

Each object constructor zeroes the first 0x5C of its owned 0x68-byte object, copies the 0x38-byte template, writes flags 1, installs its embedded tree-entry pointer and assigns the new handle before its exact initializer. The root initializer allocates/zeroes all 0x18 state bytes, then creation stores lifetime and the source scalar handle; referenceHandle, offset, cooldown and emit remain zero. Root local/world position copies source world position. Elements retain template scale Y = 1; scale X receives radial scale and scale Z receives particle scale. Renderer allocates its owned ValueTrack and later receives the owned display-list pointer. No item state or lighting allocation is performed for the new cluster, and gLiveItemCount is unchanged.

Exactly three randomBelow(360) calls occur per element, in X/Y/Z rotation order. Each advances the original four-word shared gRandomGeneratorState once and uses the unsigned result modulo 360; rotations are integers 0..359 converted to f32. Thus exactly 3 * count RNG steps occur, with no history-array or clock update. RNG state is initialized, live, disjoint and not concurrently mutated. Root/renderer initialization, frame-key evaluation and hierarchy registration introduce no extra random call.

The renderer frame-program pointer at 8006B37C is the authenticated original 8006A34C. Its first 12-byte ValueKey is mode 1, duration 0.8, start 33 and end 34; the following key is mode 3, duration -1, start -1 and end 0. Step-zero initialization writes track.time = 0, track.key = 8006A34C and track.value = 33, then returns without following the later backward jump. The final two padding bytes of the 12-byte track allocation are not initialized. The borrowed frame program remains live for later updates; its later looping behavior is outside this immediate review. No callback, RNG or allocation occurs during the integer-track evaluator itself.

particleClusterCreateDisplayList allocates count * 24 + 240 bytes and emits exactly nine leading Gfx commands, three commands per particle and three trailing commands: count * 24 + 96 bytes written, leaving 144 bytes of allocation tail untouched. Each particle command uses segmented matrix address 0x07000040 + (index << 6), segmented vertex address D_100CA98 and two fixed triangles. These are written addresses, not CPU dereferences. The retained original GBI macros and ABI have eight-byte Gfx records; every command write fits the allocation. No active global display-list cursor, texture loader, osVirtualToPhysical, GPU task or renderer draw callback is invoked. Later valid segment setup, matrices and vertex/texture resources are separate drawing prerequisites.

The root owns the linked hierarchy of count particle children followed by one renderer sibling; templates provide no extra linked nodes. objectMakeHierarchyRoot assigns root pointers and clears root-designation bit 4 throughout the N nodes, then sets bit 4 only on the root. The matrix allocator counts N and allocates one N * 128-byte block as two N * 64-byte halves. It assigns each node its distinct 64-byte slot in both halves; payload matrices are not computed or zeroed here. The root owns the original base allocation, while child pointers are interior borrowed views. No matrix-stack or scene-transform update occurs.

Active registration inserts all N object records in the object search tree, appends the root to the active-hierarchy pool and increments the global hierarchy count once. It ORs active flag 8 into the root/following root siblings; this authenticated root has no sibling, so children are not independently given that active bit by this call. The renderer is retained after the final particle; count positivity makes that link valid. No item-search or collision registration, owner transfer, message, audio, DMA, asynchronous I/O, destruction marking or resource free occurs. Later emitter updates, child updates, drawing, lifetime expiry and destructor cleanup are excluded; source and effect borrowed resources must remain live whenever those later consumers use them.

The full footprint includes source item direction fields, shared RNG words, new object/state/display-list/matrix allocations, heap metadata, object-handle pool, existing search-tree links, active pool and hierarchy-count global, plus VM stack/result and native-stack scratch. Original authenticated SDK _bzero and copy semantics apply to bounded initialization and search-tree scratch. The exact ROM templates, callback entries, frame program and math-table spans were authenticated with LocalImage and recorded in /tmp/item-particles-authenticated-resources.json. This is a complete immediate returning-path review under the stated capacities and lifetimes, not a claim that arbitrary counts, resources or later rendering are safe.
